MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 21, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
MacLean at 5:07 p.m., on September 21, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 16, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:15)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission

City Council Minutes  1  September 21, 2009
   Viejo v. Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD), Case No. 00180049;
  Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v. CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem MacLean recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:09 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Item CS1 the Council gave
instruction to move forward with settlement discussions. As those unfold, further information
will be provided. For item CS2, the City is looking to advance the meet and confer requirements
that arise under CEQA. Staff will get Council direction and will move forward accordingly.

At the Mayor’s request, Mr. Curley discussed the commencement of a CEQA action against the
Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD) relating to the closure of O’Neill School.
He provided a timeline beginning with the City’s first Public Records Act request filed with
SVUSD which established inconsistencies and uncertainties surrounding the District’s CEQA
processing and its reuse of the O’Neill Elementary School facility and the Via Fabricante
facility. Mr. Curley was instructed to communicate with the District which he did during the
Council’s summer break. In response, the District’s legal Counsel stated that they would not do
CEQA processing as they believe they are exempt from those requirements. In evaluating that
statement, Mr. Curley noted that the City Council’s first priority has always been to protect the
quality of life of its citizenry. He stated that his task is to protect the Council’s legal rights. Mr.
Curley discovered that the date of the City Council’s first meeting after its summer hiatus,
September 8, 2009, was the same date that the statute of limitations would expire.
Understanding the Council’s reaction from the July meeting and their basic process of protecting
the community, Mr. Curley believed that the better decision was to preserve the Council’s right
to consider whether they wanted to pursue environmental litigation. His office prepared and
filed the case that day but did not serve it upon the District. Upon presenting it to the Council at
the meeting on September 8, he provided the Council the opportunity to decide to pursue it or
not. Had the Council elected not to pursue the CEQA challenge, he would have withdrawn it
and sent communication to the District noting that the suit was filed prematurely. The City
would not have been charged for the costs involved if it was something the Council didn’t want.

City Council Minutes  2  September 21, 2009
 In the end, the Council instructed his office to move forward and he feels his decision was
ethically and professionally proper.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department School Resource Officers

  The Council received the presentation from Lt. Mike Gavin and Deputy Lance
  Christiansen.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

John Maginnis, M.V.: thanked the City Council for partnering with the Friends of the Mission
Viejo Library to bring forward a most extravagant and successful Readers’ Festival.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: read from a letter sent by the City Attorney to Dr. Steven Fish,
Superintendent of Saddleback Valley Unified School District, on September 8, 2009. Mr. Gilbert
asked who gave the City Attorney permission to send the letter when the Council had not already
discussed whether they wished to file a CEQA challenge regarding the O'Neill School site.

Catherine Jasper, M.V.: stated that she was disappointed with the content of the report that she
received last Friday regarding ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja Lane.

Christine Saracino, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of progress on the construction
at 26992 La Paja and she presented recent photographs of the property and the equipment being
used in the construction. She also indicated that there are new occupants in the home.

Barbara Remington, M.V.: referring to the Readers’ Festival, she stated that the City’s
commitment to the quality of life in Mission Viejo is to be commended. She thanked the Friends
of the Mission Viejo Library and the City Council for a wonderful event and she expressed hope
that it will become an annual festival.

Bob Breton, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo's events are so well planned and carried out that
other cities ask why they can’t do the same. He credited Dennis Wilberg and Valerie Maginnis
for their vision, leadership, and initiative in planning the first annual Readers' Festival. To say
that this event was successful is an understatement and the community is now becoming known
for its emphasis on education, literacy, and culture.

Terisue George, M.V.: stated that the School Resource Officers' service is invaluable. Students

City Council Minutes  3  September 21, 2009
 look up to and count on the SRO’s and she would hate to see that program eliminated from any
of our schools.

City Attorney Bill Curley responded to comments made on the La Paja Lane construction
project. He has been tasked with putting together an agreement and timeline and during the
process, further discrepancies and surprises have unfolded. Each time that occurs, the timeline is
delayed. He stated that setbacks come as a result of sorting out pre-existing defects that need to
be addressed before the timeline can be finalized.

City Manager Wilberg outlined obstacles and staff’s challenge to uncover additional problems.

Council Member Kelley asked if there is something that prohibits people from living in the home
on La Paja.

Mr. Curley stated that he wasn’t sure of the status but he thought that part of the home was
habitable.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

22.  City of Mission Viejo Saddleback Room and Friends Community Room Policies and
  Procedures

  Director of Library Services Valerie Maginnis outlined the policy for rental of the
  Saddleback Room.

City Attorney’s Report

23.  Review of background and status of environmental litigation against Saddleback
  Valley Unified School District

  This item was discussed in the Report of Closed Session (see page 2).

City Attorney Bill Curley discussed his attendance at this morning’s Sheriff’s Department
meeting regarding medical marijuana dispensaries throughout Orange County. He stated that

City Council Minutes  9  September 21, 2009
 this is an emotional issue and neighboring cities and the County are undertaking very aggressive
investigation and prosecution of dispensaries in their jurisdictions. He noted that Mission Viejo
has been fortunate to date.

Lt. Mike Gavin stated that today’s forum was brought about by the Sheriff’s Department and its
contract partners. Sheriff Hutchens felt it was necessary to include representatives from the
District Attorney’s office, Orange County Counsel, and Sheriff’s Department personnel to give
insight into the growth of the issue and how it can be addressed. Lt. Gavin stated that the
Compassionate Use Act was passed in 1996 but some of the businesses popping up in
neighboring cities are not complying with the act and it is going to be an expensive battle.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley complimented the City Manager for having the vision to plan a Readers’
Festival and she recognized the tremendous amount of initiative and work that Valerie Maginnis,
Stephanie Tanton, Toni Nunez and the library staff put into the event. She thanked artist Cindy
Jordan and the army of volunteers that turned out to help with this wonderful festival. She
invited residents who may have missed the Readers’ Festival to mark their calendars and plan to
attend next year. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the recent Chamber of
Commerce Health and Wellness program and at the Inner Coastal Cleanup Day and she stated
that she was impressed with both events. She announced that she attended the grand opening of
Rumbi Island Grill in Gateway Center on Alicia Parkway. The prices are great and she
encouraged everyone to visit the restaurant and take their families. She also encouraged
residents to visit Cafe Maiz on September 23, 2009, when the restaurant will donate 50% of their
proceeds to the City’s Marine Adoption Committee. Finally, Council Member Kelley reminded
residents that the Orange County International Triathlon will be held on Sunday, September 27,
beginning at 7:00 a.m. at Lake Mission Viejo. This event has been designated as "Best of the
US" and is quite a spectacle to see. She invited interested residents to visit http://www.octri.com
for more information and for road closure notices.

Council Member Ledesma

City Council Minutes  10  September 21, 2009
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she appreciated Lt. Gavin’s report on the School Resource
Officers (SRO’s) and she thought the presentation was brought forward because she questioned
the need for keeping the SRO’s at the schools. She stated that we are spending $1 million for
five SRO’s but we have limited funds, our contract for the Sheriff’s Department has only gone
up, and she asked when do we draw the line. Council Member Schlicht stated that the SRO’s do
a fabulous job but she is surprised we are supplying one for Tesoro High School which is outside
of the City limits. She recommended that instead of footing the entire bill, Mission Viejo could
share costs with other communities around us. She further stated that she believes cities should
not be involved in school security or school crossing guards because that is a school function.
Council Member Schlicht recommended giving money to the schools and letting them take care
of it that way. She also noted a recent email requesting a new crossing guard and she
recommended looking at all the crossing guards again to consider different options for using the
same dollars wisely. Council Member Schlicht announced that she attended a Tea Party on
September 12, 2009, and it was very well attended. She stated that she hopes the tea parties
continue so government will start learning to listen to its residents. Lastly, she noted that the
Heritage Committee is selling a neat deck of Mission Viejo cards and she encouraged residents
to seek those out.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean complimented our police officers, especially the School Resource
deputies, for all that they do. When we make a significant investment in our Sheriff’s
Department it pays dividends. Mission Viejo has long been known as the safest city in
California and one of the safest cities in the nation. We continue to win awards and keep our
community safe and our residents appreciate their quality of life. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
stated that he is very proud of the accomplishments of the Sheriff’s Department and he noted that
others look to us as a model. Our officers are training officers in other cities so they can
implement programs like ours and that speaks volumes about what we’ve accomplished.

Mayor Ury

Reminded Council Member Schlicht to put items on the agenda if she would like to address
concerns. Moving things forward is important.

25.  Expected State Borrowings and Takings of Mission Viejo Revenues in 2009-10 and
  2010-11

City Council Minutes  11  September 21, 2009
   By consensus, the City Council directed staff prepare a full report, from a legal and
  financial standpoint, as to how the City could borrow against the CDA housing fund to
  backfill for the anticipated State borrowings of City revenue.

26.  Discussion of Reinstating Items Cut From the 2009-10 Library Budget

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to reinstate
  $155,172 to the Library operating budget for reductions made during the budget process.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

27.  State Mandates

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to prepare a list of all State Mandates
  affecting Mission Viejo and how much money the City must set aside to comply. Return
  at a Council Meeting for future discussion.

Mayor Ury concurred that Valerie Maginnis, staff and the volunteers did a wonderful job with
the Readers’ Festival. He noted that we are doing roughly one special event per month and that
is nice to see.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 5, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.
